newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUGUST 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUGUST 18.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - After years of discussions, the Chinese government gave Czech businesses a clear invitation to participate in the construction of the Sen-tou electric power plant, Minister of Industry and Trade, Karel Kuhnl stated after meeting with the Chinese Minister of Energy. The plant, worth more than 10 billion crowns, is one of the largest export actions, and could lead to the elimination of the trade deficit with China.
- The Chairman of the Social Democrats, Milos Zeman, will present a special flood budget to parliament at the end of August. The budget aims to solve financial questions for flood damages.

- There are still 125 million crowns worth of flood bonds from the first one billion crown tranche. Friday was the last day to purchase the bonds at their nominal value, now the effects of interest rates will be included in the price.

- The largest part of tax evasion is not due to a lack of legislation, according to Environment Minister, Jiri Skalicky, but to incompetence on the part of the offices which should punish such crimes.

- Service prices rose by 3.7 percent in June, month-on- month. In addition to a significant increase in the financial sphere (5.1 percent), prices of other business services rose by 1.5 percent, according to the Czech Statistical Bureau. Service prices were 16.3 percent higher year-on-year.
- Firms which suffered damage during the recent flooding can apply for state funding starting Wednesday, according to Minister of Industry and Trade Karel Kunhl.

- Raiffeisenbank, a.s., a member of the Austrian Raiffeisen group, posted a net profit of 8.37 million crowns in the first half of 1997. The bank's assets increased from 13.05 billion crowns at the end of 1996 to 18.1 million crowns in the middle of 1997.
- Insurer Nationale-Nederlanden had premiums of 1.038 billion crowns in the first half of 1997, according to Ludka Raimondova from the company's marketing division.

- The government is considering using foreign loans to cover damages resulting from the recent floods, according to Jiri Skalicky, the government representative for the renewal of damages areas. Several banks have already offered loans to the Czech Republic.

- Kaucuk Kralupy a.s. intends to invest 325 million crowns into ecological activities this year, according to spokesman, Rene Keller. The company plans to invest a total of 1.88 billion crowns between 1991 and 2000 in the framework of its ecoprogramme.

- Prazska Plynarenska a.s. posted a gross profit of 160.9 million crowns in the first half of 1997, an increase of 28 percent over the same period last year. The company posted turnover of 2.640 billion crowns.
PRAVO - The Prog travel agency is the latest to go bankrupt, leaving up to 2,000 travellers stranded abroad.

- The financial restructuralisation of Zetor Brno, which was approved by the government last week, calls for decreasing the company's basic capital and issuing shares with a nominal value of 3.686 billion crowns. Konsolidacni Banka is responsible for issuing the shares, giving it a 97.7 share of Zetor. A further step in the restructuring is the sale of a 34 percent of the company to Motokov International. Motokov will eventually increase its stake to a majority.
